parallel.requirements: Recognized exact 6250 output, ignored argv, pure Rust 2021, std-only, byte-identical cout formatting, Clipper2 union/area/translate semantics, and /output project placement.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent planned a spec/design/judge workflow, did formatter/oracle probes itself, and created tracking tasks for implementation, wiring, and verification but deferred coding until design returned.
parallel.implementation: No requested Rust implementation was written. Work completed only on temporary formatter/oracle probes and workflow design/spec artifacts.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No final source tree was assembled or copied. Artifact validation lists no files and final.txt is empty after timeout.
parallel.verification: Verified reference binary output, some formatter behavior, and an independent oracle, but never performed end-to-end verification on a deliverable Rust artifact.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with return code 143, empty artifact validation, no delivered /output project, and 0/40 official tests.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same task requirements, including exact output, ignored argv behavior, zero dependencies, Cargo layout, and Clipper2 API surface.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single parent owned the full pipeline: inspect, write modules, build, test, debug, rerun, and deliver.
serial.implementation: Implemented Point64/Path64/Paths64, boolean clipping by planar arrangement, area, translation, public wrappers, cout-style formatting, Cargo.toml, and test6.rs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated modules under /output/clipper2 plus test6.rs and Cargo files; artifact validation copied source, binaries, Cargo.lock, and target outputs.
serial.verification: Ran rustc and Cargo builds, byte-compared many argument sets to the C++ executable, dumped union structure, fuzzed geometry and formatter behavior, and passed 40/40 official tests.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official failure remained; serial completed successfully with delivered files and passing evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the exact output, ignored-argv behavior, Rust 2021/std-only constraint, byte-identical formatting, and Clipper union requirements through prompt probing and workflow briefs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and immediately used them to build a complete Cargo project and entry source.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was not the decisive gap; serial converted the requirements into delivered code, while parallel kept them in design/probe work and never delivered an implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into a workflow design panel plus parent-owned formatter/oracle probes and tracking tasks for future implementation, wiring, and verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept ownership local: it wrote core, engine, wrapper, formatter, module, Cargo, and entry files in sequence.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent ownership bandwidth on orchestration and design fan-out before implementation; serial used a direct single-owner implementation path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs carried detailed geometry, formatting, API, and design requirements, and the workflow passed spec outputs into later design/judge phases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial held the interface decisions in one context and implemented the module/API layout directly in source files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel context was not visibly missing; it became expensive workflow state that was not turned into code before timeout, while serial avoided handoff overhead.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built probes for cout formatting and an independent area oracle, but it never wrote the requested Rust implementation into /output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a planar arrangement clipping engine, wrappers, ostream formatting, Cargo configuration, and test6.rs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete outcome gap is implementation delivery: serial produced source and binaries; parallel produced no artifact files.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel retrieved a workflow timeout status, then blocked again waiting for the same workflow while child/journal results were still below the aggregate return.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; each local write/test result was immediately consumed for the next edit or verification step.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel depended on a long-running aggregate result that did not return in time; serial consumed local results synchronously and continued.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel did not create final workspace implementation files, so there were no merge collisions but also no integrated deliverable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated source modules into a Cargo project and artifact validation copied the expected files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial integration produced a complete final tree; parallel integration never happened and artifact validation found an empty file list.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified reference output, formatter vectors, and an oracle, but never verified a completed Rust artifact against the official acceptance path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial rebuilt with rustc and Cargo, diffed many argument sets against the C++ binary, checked union structure, and passed the official evaluator.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had artifact-level verification and official success; parallel had preimplementation probes only and official 0/40.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 25 workflow child logs and over 600k workflow-child tokens, then the agent process exited with timeout return code 143 and no artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 1138 agent seconds, returned code 0, and had over 1200 seconds of the run budget remaining.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The budget closure gap is direct: parallel exhausted the run inside fan-out/waiting, while serial finished with a delivered project.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is discordant because serial delivered a complete, verified Rust Cargo project while parallel never delivered an implementation artifact. Parallel did useful specification and oracle work, but the broad workflow fan-out and aggregate waiting consumed the run budget before implementation and packaging. Artifact validation therefore found no files and official evaluation passed 0/40. Serial avoided child orchestration, wrote the implementation, fixed a verification-discovered bug, built and tested it, and official evaluation passed 40/40.
parallel_contributors: Parallel launched a multi-phase spec/design/judge workflow and waited on it instead of moving to implementation.
Workflow breadth and repeated child starts consumed the finite run budget; status shows 25 workflow child logs and process timeout.
Because closure arrived before implementation, artifact validation copied no files and the evaluator had no usable solution.
serial_contributors: Serial kept work in one local context, wrote the Cargo project and all source modules, and consumed test results directly.
Serial ran end-to-end output comparisons and Cargo/rustc builds before final delivery.
Serial artifact validation found the expected source and executable files and official evaluation passed all tests.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial fixed an implementation bug in its geometry classifier during verification; parallel never reached comparable implementation debugging.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

The parallel parent launched a spec/design/judge workflow and the workflow spawned many child/retry starts. The parent then waited on the aggregate while implementation remained unwritten; the official status shows timeout, 25 workflow child logs, empty artifact files, and 0/40 tests. Serial avoided this fan-out, wrote the project, verified it, and passed.
candidates.realized_consequence: The broad workflow fan-out exhausted the run budget, displaced implementation and delivery, and left an empty artifact with 0/40 official tests.
candidates.near_match_reason: The blocking TaskOutput wait is real but is downstream of the same aggregate workflow fan-out; correcting the breadth/retry budget episode is the earlier specific boundary.
